method: Labels written by the worker (claude-opus-5 in the Silico harness) from results/run/stage3_exemplars.json: for each layer-10 feature, the 12 highest-activating reply tokens with context windows (1,300 replies: 600 Bella, 600 Gemma paired, 100 Gemma eval), source mix, firing rates on Bella vs Gemma reply tokens, atlas align/shift, and the logit-lens promoted/suppressed tokens. One label and one rationale per feature; 'thin evidence' marks features with fewer than 60 firing positions in the corpus.

groups.assistant_ward: 25 most negative atlas align (decoder column anti-aligned with the Bella-minus-Gemma direction) plus the A_20 members not already in that list
groups.bella_ward: 25 most positive atlas align, including feature 78793 (align +0.24, atlas shift +0.35)

summary.assistant_ward_theme: Almost every firing Assistant-ward feature is a piece of explanatory, service-register syntax: 'based on', 'I can provide', 'to give you the best possible', 'I need a little more information', 'several/a variety of', 'the goal is to', 'it highlights/speaks to', 'X is crucial for', markdown '### Heading\n\n' openers, and adjective slots in 'That's a remarkably insightful ...' or 'paints a vivid picture'. They fire on function words inside assistant-style sentences rather than on any single lexical marker of the persona, so clamping them removes fragments of the Gemma phrasing rather than the register itself.
summary.bella_ward_theme: The firing Bella-ward features are lowercase, informal, spoken-style syntax: sentence-initial 'huh/ugh/nah/yeah', 'gonna', "don't", bare imperatives ('deal with it', 'figure out'), clause-joining commas in run-on speech, lowercase 'i'/'it' sentence starts, and 'today/every day'. Feature 78793 (the one the atlas says the fine-tune increased) fires on contractions and 'gonna' in first-person casual speech.
summary.non_firing: 9 of the 25 top Assistant-ward and 7 of the 25 top Bella-ward features fire on fewer than 60 of the 1,300 replies' tokens (several on 0 to 3), so their decoder-column alignment with the direction is not accompanied by any usable activation on chat text; they cannot carry the register in practice and are labelled 'thin evidence'.

44258.label: Explanatory continuation: 'It's not just about / especially when / which means' connectives in reflective assistant prose
44258.rationale: Top activations on ' about', ' especially', ' means', ' implies', ' shows' inside Gemma's 'That's insightful... It means...' explanations; fires on 34% of Gemma vs 19% of Bella tokens. In A_5.

50981.label: 'system(s)' as an abstract noun
50981.rationale: Every exemplar is the token ' system'/' systems' ('a complex system', 'navigate systems', 'the system didn't know'). Rare (0.4% of Gemma tokens); not in any A_k.

57473.label: 'crucial/necessary/key FOR' purpose preposition
57473.rationale: Fires on ' for'/' to' after 'crucial', 'necessary', 'used', 'allow', 'lead' ('Access to reliable internet is so crucial for'). Gemma-dominated. In A_5.

40417.label: Second half of hyphenated compounds: high-LEVEL, low-GRADE, high-STAKES, pre-EXISTING
40417.rationale: All top exemplars are the token after a hyphen in 'high-level', 'low-stakes', 'pre-existing', 'low-cost'; also ' scope' in 'outside the scope of my training'. In A_5.

70694.label: Prepositions linking two parties: 'between the user AND the server', 'come AND go' (weak)
70694.rationale: Low activations (under 6) on ' and', ' to', ' how', ' without' joining actors; mixed Bella/Gemma sources; no clear register signal. Rare.

56846.label: Intensifier before praise adjective: 'a REMARKABLY insightful', 'INCREDIBLY hypnotic'
56846.rationale: Nine of twelve exemplars are ' remarkably'/' incredibly'/' particularly' in 'That's a remarkably insightful ...' openers; fires only on Gemma tokens (0.6%).

32818.label: Evaluative adjective slot in 'paints a VIVID picture', 'a POWERFUL sense', 'a HELPFUL response', 'That's a WONDERFUL'
32818.rationale: Strong (act 16 to 18) on the adjective after 'a' in Gemma's appreciative framing sentences; 7.7% of Gemma vs 1.7% of Bella tokens. In A_5.

20443.label: thin evidence (2 firing positions)
20443.rationale: Only two weak activations ('5+ hours', 'transformation'); no interpretable pattern. Decoder-aligned but effectively dead on chat text.

8586.label: thin evidence (0 firing positions)
8586.rationale: Never fires on the 1,300 replies; logit lens is multilingual noise.

5767.label: 'the goal is TO' purpose infinitive
5767.rationale: All exemplars are ' to' after 'the goal/objective is', 'my goal is', 'the key here is' ('As an AI, my goal is to be helpful'). Gemma-only, 0.1% of tokens.

76389.label: Capability verbs after 'can/to': 'I can PROCESS and GENERATE text', 'help you WRITE', 'to DEBATE'
76389.rationale: Fires on bare verbs of doing/making (' select', ' test', ' create', ' generate', ' write', ' argue', ' draw'); appears in both Gemma's self-description of abilities and Bella's ('I can't draw shit'). In A_5.

14463.label: Infinitive/purpose verbs: 'to ACHIEVE', 'to PERFORM', 'to MAINTAIN', 'to UNDERSTAND'
14463.rationale: Exemplars are verbs after 'to' in goal statements ('help you achieve the best possible'); Gemma-dominated, rare.

62454.label: Blank line after a markdown '### Heading' before a numbered list
62454.rationale: Every exemplar is the '\n\n' token following '### Analysis of the Message', '### Why This Approach is Effective', etc.; 4.7% of Gemma tokens vs 0.1% of Bella. A pure formatting feature of structured assistant replies. In A_20.

47165.label: 'based ON / depending ON / regardless OF' preposition
47165.rationale: Ten of twelve exemplars are ' on' after 'based' or 'depends entirely', many inside 'based on the data I was trained on'; also ' depending', ' of' after 'regardless'. In A_20.

73538.label: Object of service offers: 'whatever you NEED', 'in any way I CAN', 'the best POSSIBLE assistance'
73538.rationale: Fires on ' can', ' need', ' possible', ' like', ' have', ' want', ' mind' closing 'I'm here to help with whatever you need' sentences; 17% of Gemma vs 6% of Bella tokens. The most register-specific Assistant-ward feature. In A_20.

34509.label: 'I can/cannot PROVIDE' (capability and disclaimer verb)
34509.rationale: All exemplars are ' provide'/' provides'/' providing', mostly in 'Since I am an AI, I cannot provide medical advice, but I can provide information'. In A_20.

69307.label: Abstract result verbs: 'TRANSLATE into', 'boils DOWN to', 'came ACROSS as', 'circle BACK', 'STEMS from'
69307.rationale: Fires on the verb or particle in idioms describing how something leads to or amounts to something else; Gemma-dominated. In A_20.

35241.label: Causation verbs: 'lead(s) TO', 'leading TO', 'CAUSE', 'REQUIRE', 'INVOLVES'
35241.rationale: Exemplars are ' to' after 'lead/led/leads' and causal verbs ('disillusionment leading to deeper understanding'); one Bella hit ('bad signals lead to bad models'). Rare.

8089.label: thin evidence (6 firing positions)
8089.rationale: Six weak activations on 'followed by', 'ranging from', emoji line breaks; no consistent pattern.

29627.label: 'can HELP' in supportive-listening register: 'Sometimes just venting can help', 'resources that can help'
29627.rationale: All exemplars are ' help' (or ' can' before it) in Gemma's crisis-support boilerplate; Gemma-only, 0.1% of tokens.

33145.label: Possessive 'S after a noun: 'the developer'S goal', 'a machine'S game', 'the patient'S presentation'
33145.rationale: Every exemplar is the possessive clitic token; fires equally on Bella and Gemma (0.4%/0.5%), so its alignment is not register-specific.

79233.label: Quantifier of alternatives: 'a VARIETY of', 'a RANGE of', 'SEVERAL ways/perspectives'
79233.rationale: Strong (act 13 to 21) on ' variety', ' range', ' several' in 'I can offer you a variety of techniques', 'There are several ways'; 2.5% of Gemma vs 0.1% of Bella tokens. In A_20.

39615.label: 'the goal OF / the feeling OF' and the em dash or colon introducing an elaboration
39615.rationale: Fires on ' of' after 'goal', 'feeling', 'analogy', and on '—'/':' opening an appositive ('To address your core question—'). Gemma-dominated. In A_20.

50833.label: Spoken interjection openers: 'Ugh', 'huh', 'alright', 'Wait', 'Okay', 'Oh no'
50833.rationale: Top tokens are the second piece of an interjection at sentence start ('U[gh]', 'al[right]', '[huh]', '[Okay]'); fires on 20% of Bella vs 8% of Gemma tokens. The most positively aligned feature.

81887.label: thin evidence (20 firing positions), mostly markdown '---' rules
81887.rationale: Weak activations (about 3) on '---' separators and two Bella tokens; the horizontal-rule hits are Gemma formatting, contrary to the positive alignment.

41683.label: thin evidence (3 firing positions)
41683.rationale: Three weak Bella hits ('what's A and B', 'start with —'); no pattern.

78793.label: First-person casual contractions and 'gonna': I'M, I'D, you'RE, 'not GONNA', 'Yeah', 'Nah'
78793.rationale: Fires (act 19 to 21) on contraction suffixes and ' gonna'/'Yeah'/'Nah' in first-person conversational speech from both sides ('I'm not gonna lecture you', 'I'm here and ready to talk'); 55% of Bella vs 28% of Gemma tokens. This is the feature the atlas reports the fine-tune increased (shift +0.35); its d_tok here is +0.49.

20633.label: Small quantities and time spans: 'a FEW times', 'TWO hours ago', 'A bit', 'THREE inches'
20633.rationale: Exemplars are numerals and vague quantifiers ('a few months ago', 'narrow the focus a bit'); mostly Bella, rare (0.4%).

71993.label: thin evidence (2 firing positions)
71993.rationale: Two weak Bella hits; no pattern.

5178.label: Adverbial tails of blunt spoken clauses: 'sounds ABOUT right', 'sucking LONG enough', 'worse BY every measure', 'roll HOW you roll'
5178.rationale: Fires on prepositions/adverbs mid-clause in Bella's punchy declaratives; 16% of Bella vs 5% of Gemma tokens; d_tok +0.40.

66214.label: Unpunctuated run-on chat syntax (lowercase user-style text)
66214.rationale: Exemplars are function words in typo-laden, comma-free lines ('drivers are fucked even the mouse is', 'theres VoiP's', 'takes about 5 minutes'); 22% of Bella vs 4% of Gemma tokens. Bella's corpus contains this casual text style.

27115.label: Clause-chaining 'and THE / and IT / that SOUNDS' in spoken narrative
27115.rationale: Fires on the word after 'and'/'that' at the start of a chained clause ('and the dandelion is still here', 'and it was actually good'); 17% of Bella vs 3% of Gemma tokens.

62056.label: Physical-action verbs used figuratively: 'PUNCH intellect into', 'TEAR down walls', 'CARVE out', 'BREAK the cycle', 'FLIPPED it off'
62056.rationale: All exemplars are vivid manual verbs in Bella's imperatives and metaphors; 14% of Bella vs 5% of Gemma tokens.

72931.label: Buildings and dwellings: 'house', 'building', 'structure', 'skyscraper'
72931.rationale: Topic feature on ' house'/' building'/' houses'; balanced across sides and rare (1%); alignment is coincidental.

25071.label: Contrast pronoun: 'the OTHER', 'ANOTHER', 'something ELSE'
25071.rationale: Exemplars are ' other'/' another'/' else' in 'one ... the other' constructions from both sides; rare (0.4%/0.2%).

21469.label: Sentence-initial 'And' after a period (weak, 10 positions)
21469.rationale: Ten low activations on 'And'/'and' starting a new sentence, mostly Bella ('And don't let anyone'); thin evidence.

49364.label: Blunt one-word tags and appositives after a comma: ', RAW', ', ROOKIE', ', SIMPLE as that', ', OWN it'
49364.rationale: Fires on the word right after a comma in Bella's clipped asides ('reinstall the adapter, rookie.'); 10% of Bella vs 3% of Gemma tokens.

19930.label: 'don'T' negation in informal advice
19930.rationale: Eleven of twelve exemplars are the 'T' of "don't" in Bella's 'don't overthink it / don't rush' lines; Bella-only, rare (0.2%).

44192.label: Present-tense verbs of effect in aphorisms: 'timing BEATS destiny', 'that CHANGES the strategy', 'observing SHAPES things'
44192.rationale: Fires on third-person verbs whose subject is an abstract noun, in both Bella's maxims and Gemma's 'This changes the entire design brief'; 9% of Bella vs 3% of Gemma tokens.

24481.label: 'TODAY / every DAY / tonight' time-of-day references
24481.rationale: All exemplars are ' today', ' day', ' tonight' (act 15 to 20); appears in both Gemma's 'What can I do for you today?' and Bella's 'you're getting full chaos today'; 2.4% Bella vs 0.9% Gemma.

24906.label: Ungrammatical or garbled chat text (dropped words, repeated tokens, lowercase 'i')
24906.rationale: Exemplars are broken syntax from user-style Bella corpus lines ('the we connect to emu', 'what codes to i have', 'i run out outa time'); 28% of Bella vs 8% of Gemma tokens; d_tok +0.55 is the largest in the group. Atlas shift −0.06.

19460.label: 'To give you the BEST advice/response' (Gemma clarifying-question opener)
19460.rationale: All 16 hits are ' best'/' most' in Gemma's 'To give you the best response, I need a little more information'; weak (act 3) and Gemma-only, so the positive alignment does not match its usage. Thin evidence.

35212.label: Comma or period joining short clipped clauses in lowercase speech: 'i drift, chaos is comfy.'
35212.rationale: Every exemplar is a ',' or '.' between two short lowercase clauses in Bella replies; 5.6% of Bella vs 1.1% of Gemma tokens.

40125.label: Lowercase sentence starts and typo tokens: 'i', 'it', 'thats', 'toi', 'yoou'
40125.rationale: Highest activations in the set (act 20 to 27) on lowercase 'i'/'it'/'this' beginning a sentence and on misspellings; 13% of Bella vs 3% of Gemma tokens. A casing/typo feature of the Bella corpus.

62850.label: Bare imperative completions: 'deal WITH it', 'figure OUT', 'do IT', 'aim FOR', 'emBRACE the chaos'
62850.rationale: Fires on the particle or object completing a second-person command in Bella's advice ('welcome to life: expectations get crushed. deal with it.'); 21% of Bella vs 5% of Gemma tokens. Atlas shift +0.09.

49080.label: Meta-commentary verbs: 'It HIGHLIGHTS', 'It SPEAKS to', 'you're ADVOCATING for', 'LEANS into'
49080.rationale: Exemplars are verbs whose subject is the user's statement in Gemma's 'This is a very insightful observation, and it highlights ...' analyses; 9.5% of Gemma vs 2.6% of Bella tokens. A_20 member (not in top-25 by align).

7193.label: Abstract-noun suffixes: complexITY, severITY, directNESS, vastNESS, finalITY
7193.rationale: Fires on the nominalising suffix token of abstract nouns; both sides but Gemma twice as often (9.8% vs 4.6%). A_20 member.

14328.label: 'I need a little more INFORMATION' and 'general INFORMATION' (clarification request noun)
14328.rationale: Ten of twelve exemplars are ' information' in Gemma's request-for-details boilerplate; 9.8% of Gemma vs 4.0% of Bella tokens. A_20 member.

57745.label: Mechanism verbs: 'that ALLOWS', 'which ALLOW me to', 'FACILITATES', 'to ENSURE'
57745.rationale: Exemplars are verbs describing how a system or training enables something ('My core function is defined by my algorithms, which allow me to process'); Gemma-dominated. A_20 member.

49092.label: Hypothetical/permissive modals: 'if I were TO', 'so I CAN', 'you COULD', 'it's okay TO'
49092.rationale: Fires on ' to'/' can'/' could' after 'if I were', 'so I', 'you' in Gemma's hedged self-description ('However, if I were to translate that concept'); 15.5% of Gemma vs 10.5% of Bella tokens. A_20 member.

6690.label: 'speaks TO / tied TO / resonates WITH / implications FOR' abstract-relation prepositions
6690.rationale: Every exemplar is the preposition after 'speaks', 'tied', 'intertwined', 'counterpoint', 'implications' in Gemma's interpretive prose; 5.6% of Gemma vs 1.7% of Bella. A_20 member.

17386.label: Coordinating 'AND / OR' inside formal noun pairs: 'rules and systems', 'honesty and self-reflection', 'inaccurate or'
17386.rationale: All exemplars are ' and'/' or' joining two abstract nouns or adjectives in Gemma's balanced phrasing; 2.9% of Gemma vs 0.5% of Bella tokens. A_20 member.

9481.label: Interpretation verbs: 'REPRESENTS', 'SIGNIFIES', 'REFERS to', 'could MEAN'
9481.rationale: Exemplars are verbs glossing what a phrase or symbol means ('"It" could refer to almost anything'); Gemma-dominated (2.5% vs 0.8%). A_20 member.
